What a /10 means

A /10 holds 4,194,304 addresses. Blocks this size are regional or provider aggregates and are always subdivided before use.

The prefix length is the number of leading bits that identify the network. A /10 uses 10 network bits and leaves 22 host bits, so the block contains 4,194,304 addresses. Usable hosts: 2(32−10) − 2 = 4,194,304 − 2 = 4,194,302.

Configuration examples

Cisco IOS

interface Vlan10
 ip address 10.0.0.1 255.192.0.0
!
access-list 10 permit 10.0.0.0 0.63.255.255

Juniper Junos

set interfaces ge-0/0/0 unit 0 family inet address 10.0.0.1/10

Linux

ip addr add 10.0.0.1/10 dev eth0

Addresses shown are examples from private or documentation space. Replace them with your own plan.

FAQ

How many usable hosts are in a /10?

4,194,302. A /10 has 4,194,304 addresses; the first is the network address and the last is the broadcast address, so 4,194,302 are usable.

What is the subnet mask for /10?

255.192.0.0. The wildcard mask, used in ACLs and OSPF network statements, is 0.63.255.255.
